messages:
Danielle: Customer reported a sharp increase in embeddings tail latency + intermittent 504s since yesterday's runtime deploy. CC'ing eng oncall.

Mike: Thanks — any repro or logs from the customer?

Danielle: They pasted a short log and a curl repro. Key symptoms: a lot of requests that succeed quickly, but ~1-2% of requests hit 500/504 or return an "embedding dimension mismatch" error. Happens when traffic mixes small (64-dim) and large (1536-dim) models from same client.

Danielle: curl they ran:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"open-1536","input":["..."],"client_id":"acct-123"}'
```

Danielle: Their SDK batches multiple items; they set max_batch_size=64 on client side. They say dynamic batching previously handled mixed dims fine.

Mike: Noted. What does our runtime show? oliver, any correlation with the deploy?

Oliver: Looking now — deploy-bot shows the runtime change at 2026-02-12T03:10Z (PR #2748) changed dynamic batching slotting and introduced an early-kvcache-flush optimization. I see a small bump in tail latency around that time.

Oliver: From the logs:```
[2026-02-12T03:21:16Z] shard=embeds-01 queue_wait=12ms batch_size=7 max_slot=32 routes=multi
[2026-02-12T03:21:16Z] shard=embeds-01 dynslot_assign: client=acct-123 slot=18 model=open-1536 dim=1536
[2026-02-12T03:21:16Z] shard=embeds-01 dynslot_assign: client=acct-123 slot=18 model=open-64 dim=64
[2026-02-12T03:21:16Z] ERROR: batch_dispatch: inconsistent-dim: payload dims [64,1536]
```

Sara: That log looks like two different model dims getting assigned same slot leading to a mismatch at dispatch. Dynamic slot reuse should include a model-dim key. Looks like the early-kvcache-flush change may have loosened the slot key.

Mike: Repro plan: try to simulate mixed-dim traffic with our internal loadgen and vary client-side max_batch_size/slotting. Also check auth timeouts — the customer reported occasional 401->504 transitions. Could be a request retry path interacting with batching.

Danielle: Customer willing to run a controlled repro. Steps they can run from their env:```
# 1) two loops: small and large
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"model":"open-64","input":["hello"]}' & done
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"model":"open-1536","input":["hello"]}' & done
# 2) set header X-Client-Max-Batch: 64
# 3) collect any 5xx or "dimension mismatch" errors
```

Sara: Can you also have them toggle client max_batch_size to 1 / 8 / 64 and report differences? If mismatch goes away at 1, it's batching sloting related.

Oliver: Quick mitigation while we patch: add model+dim hash to slot key server-side and disable early-kvcache-flush rollout for embeds. I can push a config flag to revert.

Mike: If we revert, we'll need to watch unit cost impact but prioritize production correctness. Can we hotfix toggle?

Oliver: Yes — pushing toggle to canary in 5m. Deploy-bot: starting rollback toggle for embeds.kvcache.flush_opt=false -> canary cluster.

deploy-bot: Toggle applied to canary (embeds-canary-1). Monitoring tails.

Danielle: Customer ran quick loop after we applied toggle and saw no 500s in ~500 requests. They still see a small tail latency jitter but nothing consistent.

Mike: Good. Next steps: (1) run internal loadgen with mixed dims and traffic shapes and capture batching decisions, (2) instrument slot-key generation to include model+dim, (3) add unit/regression test that simulates interleaved client requests, (4) coordinate with release to re-enable flush_opt after safety checks.

Sara: Also check retry logic: if a request gets Auth 401 then client retries, it may create duplicate request ids that get coalesced into same slot. Ensure slot key also includes request-id or client nonce.

Oliver: I'll collect trace ids from the logs for the failed batches and paste into this thread — trying to find matching request IDs.

Danielle: I'll keep csala updated and their engineer is available for a joint repro session tomorrow. They asked about potential billing/overcharge — we should confirm no double-charge when retries happen.

Mike: Agree—billing team, FYI: we might need to verify tokenization/charging only on successful dispatch, not on queued attempts. Danielle can loop them in.

Oliver: Found matching traces: trace=trc-8a9f... shows duplicate slot assignment within 150ms window. Attaching sample trace snippet to internal tracing UI.

Sara: I'll draft a small patch to slot-key generation and add an integration test that sends mixed dims from same client with randomized timings.

Danielle: Customer appreciated the quick canary toggle. They want a formal RCA and ETA for the patch. I'll ask for a 24-48h ETA.

Mike: ETA: patch + tests + canary rollout ~36h, full rollout after metrics stable ~72h. I'll update this thread with progress.

Oliver: Monitoring canary for next 2h, will escalate if any regressions.

Danielle: Thanks all. Customer engineer will join tomorrow 14:00 PST for repro.

Mike: Noted — set a calendar invite. tagging @sara and @oliver for follow-up. :thumbsup:
